answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
